fatal_errors: The proposed simulation-guided dealloying method does not reconstruct the reported spray-drying/thermal decomposition-reduction method.
It assumes preformed NM-HEA alloy precursors, whereas the target begins with homogeneously mixed aqueous salts that are spray-dried and reduced in hydrogen.

Selective dissolution and self-assembly are incorrectly presented as the formation mechanism; the reported mechanism is noble-metal-seeded, hydrogen-assisted reduction and incorporation of transition metals into an established lattice.
The hypothesis omits the key 300°C hydrogen reduction conditions and the composition- and temperature-dependent fcc-to-hcp transformation.
No evidence is cited to support reactive molecular dynamics, dealloying, improved atomic ordering, or catalytic enhancement.
explanation: The response recognizes the broad objective of producing high-surface-area NM-HEA three-dimensional nanoframeworks and proposes a potentially testable comparison, but it substitutes an unrelated dealloying strategy for the demonstrated SD-TDR synthesis. It misses the salt precursor preparation, spray drying, hydrogen reduction, noble-metal-mediated reduction mechanism, phase-control conditions, Pd and noble-metal-free controls, and quantitative methanol-oxidation results. Its falsification experiment is directionally sensible but underspecified and does not test the target mechanism or synthesis pathway. With no supporting evidence, the alternative remains speculative rather than a well-supported plausible alternative.
